unverifiable_exemptions: Housing restricted by deed, regulatory agreement or recorded document as affordable housing, or subject to an affordable-housing subsidy agreement
Separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management, and whose tenants received the statutory written exemption notice
Owner-occupied single-family residence renting no more than two units or bedrooms, and owner-occupied duplex
Housing where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with the resident owner
Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, RCFE and adult residential facilities; school dormitories
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to residential real property, including units in mobilehome parks, once a tenant has occupied it for 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added), except for the listed exemptions. Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt unless it is a mobilehome. The section does not apply to property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept. 1, 2019. It also does not apply to property under a later ordinance that is more protective and contains a binding finding saying so; the local ordinance applies instead. A less protective local ordinance adopted after Sept. 1, 2019 is not enforced while this section is in effect.
coverage.owner_conditions: The separately alienable property exemption requires a non-REIT, non-corporate owner and the statutory notice. Owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms are exempt. Owner-occupied duplexes are exempt while the owner remains in occupancy and neither unit is an ADU or JADU.
coverage.other_conditions: Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome (subd. (l)).
